title: Search a binary search tree
summary: Why a search looks at one path from the root instead of every node.

checkpoints.text: Looking for 60. The search starts at the root, 50, like every search in a binary search tree.
60 is larger than 50, so 60 can only be in the right subtree. The whole left side (20, 30, 40) is skipped.
60 is smaller than 70, so the search turns left.
Found after looking at only three of the seven nodes. Each comparison throws away half of what is left.
Now looking for 65: 50, then 70, then 60. 65 is larger than 60, so the search goes right once more.
`cur` fell off the tree: 60 has no right child, so 65 is not in the tree. Again only one path was checked. In a balanced tree of a million values that path is about 20 nodes long.
